claims.text: Molecular dynamics simulations can be used to tune the magnetic behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Molecular dynamics simulations can be used to tune the magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Systematically varying alloy composition is the means by which molecular dynamics simulations tune magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior.
The proposed intervention is to conduct molecular dynamics simulations across different compositional variants.
The simulations are to be performed using low-dimensional configurations relevant to magnetocaloric applications.
Composition changes affect atomic interactions and atomic arrangement within the alloy.
Changes in atomic interactions influence the magnetic properties of the alloy.
Changes in atomic interactions influence the magnetocaloric response of the alloy.
Specific simulated compositional changes will alter the magnetic properties.
Specific simulated compositional changes may enhance magnetocaloric behavior.
The proposed hypothesis is limited to non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
The nature and magnitude of the magnetic and magnetocaloric effects depend on the specific compositions examined.
